newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish inflation ends 1996 below target.
newsitem.headline: Spanish inflation ends 1996 below target.

text.p: Spanish inflation moderated in December to end the year at 3.2 percent, well beneath the government's early target of 3.4 percent.
But even though further improvement is expected ahead, economists believe the Bank of Spain will refrain from cutting its key money market rate at Thursday's regular repurchase tender.

"It is a close call," HSBC James Capel analyst Gwyn Hacche told Reuters Financial Television. "But they cut fairly recently and my feeling is they will hold off until we get the fall in January inflation figures published in mid-February."

The Bank of Spain reduced it key money market rate last year to 6.25 percent from nine percent, with a final 50 basis point reduction on December 13, as inflation declined 1.2 percentage points over the course of the year.
Overall, Spanish inflation rose 0.3 percent month-on-month for 3.2 percent year-on-year unchanged from November.
Economists pointed to particular improvement in underlying inflation, which strips away volatile food and energy factors, and paints a clearer picture of the trend.
Underlying inflation rose 0.3 percent mont-on-month for a 3.0 percent year-on-year rate.

"I would emphasise the favourable evolution of underlying inflation that has fallen over the whole year by 1.8 points to 3.0 percent. The fact that the number was expected doesnt take away any of its merits," said Carmen Hernansanz of Merrill Lynch.
